| [ADR-042](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-042.md) | A kind field on CASE, from a closed vocabulary of six, so that a proposed study, a thought experiment, a formal construction and a real specimen are told apart by something other than how much of each is fact | The owner asked whether the record could type its cases: "proposed empirical experiments vs thought experiments vs. steel-man vs. etc". | [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md) v2 | A warrant field on CLAIM, saying how a claim is supported (demonstrated, empirical, interpretive) apart from whether the record accepts it and in whose voice, piloted before it is required | The owner, at U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-14, on the assistant's line "what we've demonstrated by construction, what we've made plausible through examples, and what still requires empirical evidence": "do we have anything like this already segregating CLAIMs? if not, we should consider adding it." Rejected: keeping `information-retrieval`, whose blurb is relevance and ranking; and a narrower `data-structures`, which leaves out physical design and views. | Active |
| [ADR-046](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-046.md) v2 | A TERM may be Proposed, and rival, complement or narrow another | A TERM's status is the standing of its definition, not a credence: a Proposed term is a definition recorded and not adopted. TERM gains the relations the record already uses elsewhere: `rivals` (symmetric, THEORY's from [ADR-022](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-022.md)), for definitions that cannot both be adopted for one use; `complements` (symmetric, CLAIM's from [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)), for definitions in force side by side; and `refines`/`refined_by` (QUESTION's), for a special case that stays in force. `supersedes` is kept for an adoption that retires the earlier term. Applied to [TERM-050](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md)/[TERM-061](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-061.md) (complements) and [TERM-010](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-010.md)/[TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) (refines, in place of a `supersedes` that retired nothing). Rejected: new relation names (`proposes_for`, `alternatives_to`), a separate CONCEPT scheme, a TERM-only status vocabulary, and keeping candidate definitions in prose. | Active |
| [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 | Promotion is audited in small persisted batches, ranked by expected yield, with decisions recorded apart from status changes | The owner's procedure of 2026-10-19 for finding entries whose evidence has outgrown their status. Candidates are triaged from metadata by a rubric that sets review order and never standing. They are reviewed five at a time, and each review ends in one of six dispositions with a specific blocker. Every step is persisted in record/promotion-audit/: a versioned queue.yaml with a hand-off block, one decision file per candidate, and one file per batch. A check keeps the queue and the decision files in step. Status changes go in separate pull requests of at most three entries. Rejected: one large audit held in a conversation, which is lost when the session is; a queue derived only from the decision files, which cannot say what is in progress; and promoting in the same step as reviewing. | Superseded — by [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); Superseded on 2026-10-27 by the owner's acceptance of [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md), which derives the worklist from the record on each pass instead of keeping a queue. The three evidence rulings of versions 2 to 4 stand under it. |
| [ADR-048](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-048.md) | Nucleation files any work the owner wants here; whether a work is also held in the anthology is the anthology's question | The boundary [ADR-001](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-001.md) set is dropped on the nucleation side. A work goes here when the owner wants it here, whether or not an anthology topic could hold it, and nothing is checked against the anthology before filing. Instructions for machine-learning practice still belong to the anthology, which keeps that job. An ANTH- code is cited when it is known and is no longer required. Whether a work here is also held there is for the anthology to find out. The anthology-candidate flag is still applied. | Active |
| [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) v2 | A QUESTION is Answered by an Active CLAIM or THEORY, and a partly answered question is split into an Answered child and a narrowed Open parent | An Active THEORY is the record's current account, so it can answer a QUESTION as an Active CLAIM can. A CLAIM is not filed only to restate what a reading already establishes. A question is Answered when its Active answerers, alone or together, answer it as posed and in its full scope. When they answer only part of it, the answered part is filed as a child QUESTION that refines the parent and is marked Answered. The parent is reworded to what is left and stays Open. Rejected: requiring an Active CLAIM, which makes the record assert in its own voice what it relies on others to justify; marking a partly answered question Answered; and reframing the parent into new questions. | Active |
| [ADR-050](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-050.md) v2 | A claim that calls something organized, a perspective, an agent, effective, exhausted, constituted or grounded says which sense, target or criterion it means | The perspective line's conclusions turn on distinctions the prose keeps locally and the vocabulary does not enforce: structure against efficacy, efficacy against competence and legitimacy, explanatory sufficiency against constitution, a perspective against an agent. A proposal the owner relayed on 2026-10-22 asked for a small grammar of these words, not a term for each. The decision, Proposed, is a usage protocol: each flagged word in a claim, question, term or reading must name its sense, target or criterion where it carries a substantive inference, though not in unambiguous ordinary uses. Two words get terms of their own (organization, [TERM-074](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md); perspective, [TERM-072](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-072.md)); the rest are handled here. It is prose for now, and becomes a lint pattern only if the owner adopts it. | Deferred |
| [ADR-051](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-051.md) | A CASE names where the record got it: `reported_in` links it to the work, reading or account that reports it | A documented CASE usually comes from somewhere: a paper that reports a study, a reading that describes an episode, an account whose result the case records. The record had no field for that. A CASE could support a CLAIM but not point to a LIT, NOTE or THEORY, so its provenance lived in prose. At the owner's direction (2026-10-23), CASE gains `reported_in`, naming LITs, NOTEs and THEORYs, with the converse `reports` on each. It records provenance, not support. | Active |
| [ADR-052](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-052.md) | The record's own argument is stated ordinally first: orderings, partial orders and classes before scales, a numerical measure only with what it is cardinal in stated, and incomparability or partial identification reported as a result, not a gap | Three lines reached the same method separately: freedom of will as a partial order ([CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md)), frustration as an ordinal complex ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and valence as an ordinal potential fixed up to a class ([TERM-077](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-077.md)). Each came from the owner's correction of 2026-10-17, "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure", and each was paid for when a measure was used before its cardinality was stated: two reviews of the valence line found Hodge measures reversing ordinal facts. At the owner's direction (2026-10-23) the method is recorded as a rule for the record's own argument. Rejected: leaving it to each claim, and a scale-first default with ordinal statements as a fallback. | Active |
| [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md) v3 | A LIT whose lawful free copy was located but could not be fetched by this client is Unfetched, not Unavailable | [ADR-041](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md) gave one word, `Unavailable`, to two cases: no lawful copy was found, and one was found that this client could not fetch. It weighed a separate word for the second case and declined it because "eight entries do not justify a sixth status". On 2026-10-25 the owner supplied two such works by hand and asked for a status for "content that would be easy for me to access where you encountered obstacles". A triage of the 140 `Unavailable` notes that record an access obstacle found 43 in the second case. This decision proposes a new LIT status, `Unfetched` ("Copy found, not fetched"), whose status note must give the copy's address, so that the generated status page is the owner's queue. 37 entries would move. The paywalled and the unlocated would stay `Unavailable`. | Active |
| [ADR-055](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-055.md) | endosymbiosis joins the topics | `endosymbiosis` joins the topics, labelled "Endosymbiosis and reductive evolution". It covers how a partner comes to live inside another and depend on it, and how that ends: reductive genome evolution and the dependencies it creates, including in free-living microbes; complementary loss across partners; gene transfer to the host and protein import; organellogenesis and organelle loss; eukaryogenesis; and host control of symbiont transmission. It enters with the thirty-five works registered from the exchange of 2026-10-27 on the record's coverage. The owner asked for it (2026-10-27). `ecology` keeps symbiosis as an ecological interaction. Rejected: holding the works under `ecology` and `natural-sciences`, and separate `reductive-evolution` and `organelle-evolution` words. | Active |
| [ADR-056](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-056.md) v2 | A TERM says what job its definition does (disambiguation, construct, criterion or position), piloted on a sample before it becomes a field, and a criterion TERM carries an application contract that keeps its criterion apart from its indicators | The owner, U12 of the exchange of 2026-10-26: "I feel like we need a lot of our TERMs to be like this, maybe this is a particular 'kind' within the TERM schema we should distinguish." A12 proposed four kinds, a TERM that separates senses, one that introduces a theoretical object, one that states when a concept applies and one that names a position, with an application contract for the third. Proposed, and not yet a schema change: the kinds are piloted on a sample first, as CASE's were under [ADR-042](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-042.md), and the field says what a definition does, never whether it is true or adopted. | Rejected |
| [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) v8 | Status review is ranked by reliance, derived from the record each pass, covers relations as well as statuses, and changes status in the pull request that decides it | The owner, 2026-10-27, after asking for status changes and relation changes on claims "that a lot of interesting downstream material depends on": the record had changed materially since the promotion audit of [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) stopped, and its process would benefit from changing. The audit never reached those claims: 15 of the 19 most-relied-on Proposed entries never entered its queue, its decision files went stale (230 of 308), and its owner questions sat unasked in a hand-off string. This decision replaces the procedure. A worklist is derived from the record's frontmatter on each pass and kept nowhere. It ranks Proposed entries by how much rests on them, and it lists credence inversions, retired premises and Open questions with an Active answer. A pass reviews a load-bearing entry together with the premises and objections that hold it back. It changes statuses and relations in its own pull request, records its reasoning on the entries and in one workbench entry, and puts its owner rulings in the pull request as a checklist. [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s three evidence rulings stand. Rejected: resuming the old queue, which would re-rank a record a third larger by a rubric that ranked these claims last; keeping per-code decision files, which drift from the entries they judge; and separate promotion pull requests, which took about 140 pull requests over three days and left five decided promotions undone. | Active |
| [ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md) | A THEORY can corroborate a CLAIM: evidence the record links to its own claim without the claim resting on it is corroborated_by, not grounds | The third status review ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) read the record's 38 credence inversions. These are Active claims whose `grounds` or `rests_on` named a Proposed entry. In nearly all of them the claim did not need the entry. The edge had been added later as evidence ("evidence now linked"), as an instance, or for a quotation. The record had nowhere else to put a reading that bears on a claim without being a premise of it: `corroborates` ([ADR-044](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-044.md)) runs only from claim to claim, and `complements` likewise. So readings landed in `grounds`, which says the claim stands on them, and the status check then read a Proposed reading as a missing premise. This decision lets a THEORY corroborate a CLAIM. `corroborated_by` on a CLAIM takes a THEORY as well as a CLAIM, and a THEORY gains `corroborates`. A reading the claim needs stays in `grounds`. A reading cited only for an attribution or a quotation takes no edge, because the body's citation is the link. Rejected: dropping the edges, which loses that the evidence was linked; and a new general `cites` relation, which would duplicate what a body citation already records. | Active |
| [ADR-059](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-059.md) | A status is credence in the entry's own content: an ARG's is in its inference, within the limits its undercutters grant, and a conceded objection is recorded by revising its target, not by holding the objection | Two rulings of the third status review turned on one question. Do the status words, which mean credence for a CLAIM, mean the same thing for an ARG and for a conceded counter? The owner: "my mental model is that an ARG is similar to a CLAIM, but it's clearly not so similar that we didn't collapse the distinction, so maybe using the same CLAIM.status interpretations is setting us up for problems". And of [CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md): "it's a concession, so we want to treat it as true at least within a particular context, but it might incidentally bear on other parts of the epistemic state incorrectly". Proposed: every status is credence in what the entry itself asserts. A CLAIM asserts a proposition. An ARG asserts an inference: that its premises, if held, carry its conclusion, within the limits its `undercut_by` claims grant. That the argument is sound (an Active inference with every premise held) is derived and never filed. A conceded counter is recorded by revising its target, and the counter's own status stays its credence. Rejected: reading an ARG's status as "its premises are held", which duplicates its premises' statuses; and keeping "a conceded counter goes Active", which lets a concession made in one exchange raise the credence of everything that cites the counter. | Active |
| [ADR-060](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-060.md) v2 | A claim or account that bears on a question without answering it says bears_on, and answers is for an answer, held or offered | The third status review ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) found 34 Open questions with Active answerers, and under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) none of the 102 edges settled a part of its question exactly. They were evidence, premises, sufficient cases for which-questions, or results for one model class. `answers` was the only relation from a claim or account to a question, so filing used it for "bears on" too. The owner: "split the relation ... the jobs filing onto the record clearly want one, and `answers` is not it." A CLAIM or THEORY now has `bears_on` (QUESTION), with the converse `bearing`. `answers` means an answer to the question as posed: held if Active, offered if Proposed. A part that is settled exactly is split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). The 102 Active edges are moved. The 240 edges from Proposed entries on Open questions are left for review, because whether an offered entry would answer if held needs reading. Rejected: a qualifier on `answers`, which would make every consumer read two cases out of one relation. | Active |
| [ADR-061](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md) | An ARG is any claim about support; a claim about what a source says is a THEORY | Drafted 2026-10-26 under a number main had already given another decision; refiled 2026-10-28 against the record as it now stands. [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) filed an ARG only when something had to point at an inference, and none has been filed since 2026-10-10. In that time the inference objections it was built for kept coming, filed as CLAIMs. A reading of all 453 claims found 42 whose subject is whether one entry supports another, and 17 more that bundle such a verdict with a claim about the subject matter. The boundary is redrawn by subject. CLAIM holds what the record says about its subject matter. ARG holds what it says about support, a negative verdict included: "X does not show Y" is the ARG from X to Y, Rejected, with its critical questions answered in the body. `undercuts` narrows to a claim about the subject matter that defeats an inference. A claim whose subject is what a source says becomes a THEORY, but most such claims turned out to correct a claim's use of a reading the record already holds, so they split into a THEORY revision and a Rejected ARG. Two argument forms are added, evidence and source. A support claim that Active claims rest on is split, not superseded: `rests_on` names only claims, so its subject-matter part stays a claim. Rejected: folding ARG into CLAIM, a voice field on ARG, more CLAIM schemes split by role or warrant, and leaving the boundary where it is. | Active |
| [ADR-062](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-062.md) | social-identity and altruism join the topics | Two topic words join the closed vocabulary. `social-identity` takes the psychology of group membership: social identity and self-categorization theory, identification, intergroup relations, rivalry and fandom. It enters with the self-categorization and fandom readings of 2026-10-28 and 29, which had only `social-science`. `altruism` takes whether action can aim at another's good rather than one's own. It enters with the owner's thesis that there is no selfless action, only self-interest on a larger self, and the works filed for it. The owner asked for the vocabulary to be expanded where merited. Rejected: putting both under `social-science`, or the first under `social-ontology` and the second under `moral-psychology`. | Active |
| [ADR-063](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-063.md) | future-generations joins the topics | One topic word joins the closed vocabulary. `future-generations` takes what the living owe, and why they care about, people who will live after them: longtermism and existential risk, intergenerational justice, the non-identity problem and person-affecting views, population ethics, discounting, and the psychology of concern for the future (legacy, generativity, symbolic immortality, continuity with one's future self). It enters with the legacy works of 2026-10-29 and the owner's request to extend that line to obligations toward the future. Rejected: leaving them under `ethics`, `altruism` and `motivation`, or naming the word `longtermism`. | Active |
| [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) | Copies of published articles on course, faculty and scholarly third-party pages count as lawful copies to read | The first pass over the Deferred LITs on 2026-10-29 read two works from copies on university course or group pages, and turned down similar copies of ten others as being "of unknown provenance". The owner ruled the refusals mistaken. A copy of a published article on a university course or reading-list page, a faculty or research-group page, a scholarly third-party site, or an author's upload counts as a lawful copy to read. Shadow libraries and uploads of whole in-copyright books still do not. This narrows [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)'s "an upload whose uploader is unknown". | Superseded — by [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md); Superseded on 2026-11-06 at the owner's instruction by ADR-074, which keeps this rule unchanged and moves it into the read-and-file skill's reader brief, after briefs that narrowed it filed located copies Unavailable. |
| [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) | A reading's promote_when asks only for what its title asserts | A THEORY's promote_when asks for exactly what its title asserts, at filing and at review. A title that reports what a source proposes, argues or finds, or what one study measured with the study's own hedges kept, goes Active once its source is read in full and nothing in the record contradicts the report. A demand for replication, an independent test or the version of record of a copy already read moves to a QUESTION, or, where the source asserts the wider thesis, to a Proposed THEORY that extends the entry and keeps the old condition. A proof a reading re-derived counts once a second checker has gone through it. The survey of 2026-10-30 found about 58 of 597 Proposed readings whose conditions exceed their titles; general titles keep their strict conditions. Rejected: loosening conditions across the board, which would collapse the difference between reading a source and believing it; and leaving the rule where it was, in superseded [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s text, which intake did not apply. | Active |
| [ADR-066](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-066.md) | control-theory joins the topics | One topic word joins the closed vocabulary. `control-theory` takes the analysis and design of feedback: stability and Lyapunov certificates, invariance, viability and barrier certificates, input-to-state stability and small-gain conditions, contraction, adaptive, dual and safe control, and controller synthesis under constraints. It enters at the owner's word, after the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" leaned on these tools across six turns with nowhere to file them. Rejected: leaving them under `mathematics` and `complex-systems`, and a broader `systems-theory`. | Active |
| [ADR-067](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-067.md) | line takes several values in every scheme, and CASE and ARG require it | The `line:` field holds several values wherever a scheme declares it: QUESTION, CASE, TERM and ARG now follow CLAIM, which already did. CASE and ARG now also require it, as QUESTION and CLAIM did; TERM does not. The nine CASEs without a line got theirs from the graph: the lines of the entries they are joined to. Both changes are the owner's word, given 2026-11-01. Rejected: keeping one line outside CLAIM and recording the others in prose, which hid an entry from a line it bears on. | Active |
| [ADR-068](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md) v2 | Reading and filing follow a written protocol: its invariants are held in this decision, and its steps in a skill that changes with practice | The record takes in reading through a practice of eleven steps: intake, a check against the record, identifiers, registration, a lawful copy, reading, verification, filing the reading, filing the argument, accounting for everything, and acknowledgement. Until now it lived in session memory and in the pieces [ADR-002](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md), [ADR-008](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-008.md), [ADR-041](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-041.md), [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md), [ADR-054](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-054.md), [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md) and [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) decided one at a time. Each session rebuilt it, and applied it unevenly ([ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md)'s case). This decision fixes the eight invariants. The steps go in `.claude/skills/read-and-file/SKILL.md`, edited in the pull request whose work shows a step wrong. Rejected: leaving the practice unwritten; writing every step into an ADR, which would make each refinement a supersession; a section of CLAUDE.md, which is a map and not a manual; a page under docs/, which is generated; and building it into luria before the steps have settled. | Proposed |
| [ADR-069](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-069.md) | A Read note on a work marked Unavailable, Unfetched or Deferred fails lint | Three pattern checks join `lint.fail_on`: a NOTE with status `Read` whose `paper:` is a LIT marked `Unavailable`, `Unfetched` or `Deferred`. `Read` says the full text was read closely; the first two LIT statuses say no full text was reached, and `Deferred` that the work was not read closely enough to place. None can hold beside it. A `Skimmed` note on such a work is not flagged, because a précis or an introduction is a skim of an unreached work. The record has no match today, so the checks fail on the first one. The owner asked for the rule on 2026-11-01. Rejected: flagging every note on an unreached work, which would have flagged eight honest skims. | Active |
| [ADR-070](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-070.md) | The record's process-to-process "endorsement" is split and renamed: any effect on another process's future influence is conferral, conferral through a maintained relation is a grant, and "endorse" is left to the reflective sense | [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md) named any effect one process has on another's share of future influence "endorsement". Readers took the word in its reflective, Frankfurtian sense, and an attitude and an effect on influence come apart, so one word named two things the record keeps apart. At the owner's decision, [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md) is Superseded by two terms: conferral ([TERM-103](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-103.md)), its definition renamed, and grant ([TERM-101](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-101.md)), A14 §4's narrowing to conferral that runs through a maintained relation, which the owner adopted. "Endorse" is left to higher-order volition ([TERM-102](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-102.md)). Rejected: keeping the word with a stricter definition; splitting without renaming; renaming without the narrowing. | Active |
| [ADR-071](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-071.md) v2 | Each logical unit of work goes on its own branch and its own pull request, cut from the default branch | A session given one designated branch had been putting everything on it, so one pull request (dmarx/nucleation#397) came to hold a luria pin, configuration, two syntheses, an exchange's filing and a vocabulary change. At the owner's instruction, each logical unit of work now gets a branch of its own, cut from the default branch, and a pull request of its own. A decision goes with a demonstration of its effects: the pull request that proposes it carries its first application, which is where it is approved and where git blame later finds what it changed. Rejected: one branch per session; one branch for everything; leaving it to whatever branch a session was started on; a decision alone in its own pull request. | Active |
| [ADR-072](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md) | The second-time rule governs the record's process, not its insights: a decision or principle gets written down when its occasion recurs, while an idea a source surfaces is filed when it has content of its own and the record does not already hold it | [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) made "a thing gets a code the second time it turns up" the record's filing rule for its own argument, as a throttle on agents flooding the record. The rule's home is the working agreement Luria inherits, where a hazard that catches you twice is a bug report about the workflow, and a design principle is written after its second instance. Applied to insights, it held back ideas that turn up once in one reading and are worth having. At the owner's direction, the rule now governs the record's process documents (ADRs and DPs) only. An idea a source surfaces gets a code when it has content of its own and is not already held. Passing mentions stay in their NOTE. Rejected: keeping the rule for insights; dropping the throttle altogether; a count other than two. | Active |
| [ADR-073](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-073.md) | Two new lines of inquiry, readiness and realizability, for the argument filed from the readiness, constraint-architecture and realizability syntheses, so that each can be set aside as a whole | The filings of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 in dmarx/nucleation#401 added 89 claims, questions, cases, terms and an argument of the record's own argument, filed under distributed-agency or will-organization as the nearest lines, though neither describes them. Two substantive arguments run through them, and either could be set aside without the other: what it takes to keep, reach and pay for rarely used capacities (readiness), and what a constrained system can realize, reach, tell apart and become under resource bounds (realizability). Decided: add both lines; re-tag the 89 entries, replacing distributed-agency and will-organization except where an entry concerns how an organized whole forms or governs itself; keep formal-apparatus on the general results ([ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md)); give an entry both new lines where it spans them. Proposed by the assistant on the owner's question "should we maybe add one or more new lines of inquiry here?", approved: "go ahead, put both lines in 401". | Active |
| [ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md) | Copies of published articles on course, faculty and scholarly third-party pages count as lawful copies to read, and every reading brief states which copies count and how a blocked one is filed | Supersedes [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md), on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-06. [ADR-064](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-064.md)'s rule stands unchanged: a copy of a published article on a course or reading-list page, a faculty or research-group page, a scholarly third-party site, or an author's upload is a lawful copy to read, and shadow libraries and uploads of whole in-copyright books are not. Its last consequence, that reading briefs say this, was not enough. On 2026-11-05 the lead's own briefs narrowed the rule to the author's, the publisher's or a repository's copy, and a dozen works were filed `Unavailable` where a lawful copy had been located. This decision moves the rule from the lead's discretion into the reader's brief that the read-and-file skill fixes. Every brief carries the admitted and excluded copies and [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md)'s line between `Unfetched` and `Unavailable`. A narrower brief has to say so in the curation entry, with its reason. A reader reports every copy it located, with the address and what stopped it. A refusal by the session's own permission system or network policy is an obstacle of this client. The work is then `Unfetched`, and the refusal is never worked around. | Active |
| [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) v4 | A synthesis in a filed source is audited and, when it integrates, filed as a thesis claim with its components mapped, rather than mapped to its source turns and left | Filing has treated a source's syntheses (executive summaries, positive accounts, recaps, "refreshed syntheses") as recaps: each item is mapped to the turn it came from, and the synthesis is left. That finds new content but leaves the integration with no address. So the record can't say what its current account is, and later syntheses can't be checked for drift. The exchange "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" produced four summaries of the record's account. They recast the owner's prompts as the argument's own logic and dropped two of the owner's contributions, and nothing on the record could catch it. This decision adds a synthesis audit to the read-and-file skill: find every synthesis, group its versions, classify it as descriptive, supposed or proposed, map its components to codes, and check attribution, coverage, fidelity, standing and integration. The latest version of each distinct proposed or supposed thesis is filed as one CLAIM, with its components in `rests_on` or the body, and revised in place when it returns. A synthesis is admitted as an independent hypothesis, a derived result or an explanatory integration, each with its own test (versions 2 and 3). Rejected: a new scheme for positions, until a synthesis CLAIM strains; filing every version; and the status quo. | Proposed — Amended by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md): a SYNTHESIS is an account, and whatever adds to its components is a CLAIM. Steps 1 to 4 apply to accounts and to a source's syntheses as before; step 5's admission routes are now the test a claim whose premises are claims passes to show it has content of its own, filed under [ADR-072](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md)'s rule. |
| [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) v3 | Syntheses get a scheme of their own, SYNTHESIS, with statuses about the integration, a closed admission route, components whose standing is derived, and a generated current-account view | A synthesis filed as a CLAIM strains the CLAIM scheme four ways. Its components' voice and standing live in prose and drift. Its admission route has no field. CLAIM's status vocabulary has no word for "exhausted by its components", so the first synthesis that failed admission was marked Rejected, which says false. And nothing renders the record's current account, which the owner wants. This decision adds a SYNTHESIS scheme. It keeps three judgements apart: a status for the integrating account (Current, Proposed, Rejected, Superseded); an `admission` field (admitted or unadmitted), saying whether it earned an entry; and relations for its components. It has a closed `route`, required while admitted,: hypothesis, derived or integration. It has `integrates` and `premises` relations, whose targets' standing a generated view derives. The view, docs/current-account.md, is a Jinja template that sets out every Current or Proposed synthesis by line, with each component's status read from the component when the page is built. The five syntheses filed from "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" are moved into it as the demonstration, and their CLAIMs are Superseded by the new entries. ARG's `concludes` accepts a synthesis. Rejected: a route field on CLAIM; a CLAIM-only status vocabulary; DP's document rendering; the status quo. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
| [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) | A claim moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme keeps its standing and its relations: an admitted Active claim becomes a Current synthesis, and the scheme gains grounds, uses and corroborated_by so that nothing is dropped | The first synthesis review admitted [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) and could not move it. A review files every synthesis as Proposed, so an Active claim would have been demoted, and SYNTHESIS lacked grounds, uses and corroborated_by, so moving it would have dropped its readings, terms and corroboration. This decision amends [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) and the review's decision. A move keeps the claim's standing: an admitted Active CLAIM becomes a Current SYNTHESIS and a Proposed one stays Proposed, since the move changes the scheme that holds the entry, not the record's credence in it. The scheme gains the three fields, with their converses widened to match. A review still never sets a new synthesis Current. Its demonstration is [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)'s move. Rejected: moving as Proposed and asking for re-adoption; exempting adopted claims from the move; the owner setting each moved synthesis Current by hand. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
| [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) | The record is reviewed periodically for synthesis opportunities: CLAIMs that are syntheses filed as claims are moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme, and integrations whose parts the record holds are filed when they pass admission | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) audits the syntheses a source brings, and [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) gives them a scheme and a current-account view. Neither looks at what the record already holds. Some CLAIMs are syntheses filed before the scheme existed, [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) among them. Some integrations sit in the record as parts, such as `complements` clusters, questions with several answers and deep chains, that no entry states. This decision adds a periodic synthesis review, carried by the `synthesis-review` skill. Its first stage is mechanical: scratch/formal/synthesis_candidates.py ranks candidates in two arms, migration and opportunity, and decides nothing. A reviewer then shortlists a dozen at most, preferring in-force components and lines the current-account view does not cover. Each is audited with [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s five checks and admitted by one of its three routes or not at all. An admitted migration moves into the scheme, with its relations audited. An admitted opportunity is filed as a Proposed SYNTHESIS in the assistant's voice. Nothing is set Current, and what is not admitted is recorded with its reason. Rejected: reviewing only at filing time; filing every candidate the ranking finds; leaving the sweep ad hoc. | Proposed — Amended by ADR-084: the review's arms are now coverage of each scope by an account, claims that only map their components (Arm A), and integrations held in parts, filed as claims when they pass ADR-075's test (Arm B); the synthesis-review skill carries them. |
| [ADR-079](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-079.md) | Each directed relation is stored on one side only, the side a filer writes, and its converse is derived when the record is read; the sweep that removes the stored converses is this decision's demonstration | Every directed relation in the record was stored twice, once on each end, and `luria link --fix` kept the second copy in step. About 2,770 values in 1,260 entries were such copies. Adding a relation to a new scheme, as the SYNTHESIS scheme needed, meant widening the stored converse on every target scheme. luria 1.10.0, which CI pins, can mark one side of a pair `derived`: only the other side is written, readers compute the converse, and `luria repair` moves anything written on the derived side to the primary side of the other entry. This decision marks the derived side of every directed pair, 32 field declarations, choosing the side the config's own blurbs already describe as written by `luria link --fix`. Symmetric relations (`complements`, `rivals`, `compared_against`) stay as they are, since luria never derives them. Rejected: keeping both sides; choosing the derived side pair by pair on a different principle; a partial switch. | Proposed |
| [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md) | A claim's rests_on may name a SYNTHESIS, so a claim whose premise moved into that scheme keeps its dependency; the argument chain walks the claim-to-claim steps through a pattern | Two synthesis reviews moved claims into the SYNTHESIS scheme that other live claims rested on: [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) on [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md), and [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) on [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md). A claim's `rests_on` accepted only CLAIMs, so those dependencies stayed on Superseded entries. This decision lets a claim's `rests_on` name a SYNTHESIS, with SYNTHESIS gaining the derived converse `supports`. The `argument` chain walked `rests_on`, and a luria chain stays within one scheme. So the chain now walks a named pattern, `rests_on_claim`, the claim-to-claim steps, in its place. Its demonstration repoints [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) and [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md). Rejected: leaving the dependencies on Superseded claims; a separate field such as `presupposes` for a dependency on a synthesis; replacing the chain with a hand-written view. | Superseded — by [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) |
| [ADR-081](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-081.md) | The Pages site deploys at most once every two hours: a merge still triggers it, a gate skips the build when the last deploy is under two hours old or already published the commit, and a scheduled run every two hours publishes what the gate skipped | Every Docs run on main triggered a full Pages build, and the build takes a long time. Merges come in runs, so most builds were superseded before they finished. A gate job now reads the last deploy to the `github-pages` environment. It skips the build when that deploy is under two hours old, or when it already published the commit; a manual run always builds. A scheduled run every two hours applies the same gate, so a skipped merge is published by the next one, at most about two hours late. Rejected: a schedule alone, which drops publish-on-merge; a concurrency group alone, which still builds after every merge; and counting the workflow's own runs, which would count the runs the gate skipped. | Proposed |
| [ADR-082](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) v2 | The nucleating-argument line is split in three: nucleating-argument keeps how an argument drifts, anchors and pays for anchoring; what a record of inquiry keeps and the record as its own apparatus become lines of their own, because their parts barely relate to the rest | The nucleating-argument line's first account ([ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md)) fell into five parts. Counting the relations among their components showed three of them, drift, anchors and the costs of anchoring, linked densely to each other. The other two barely linked to anything. "What a record of a developing argument keeps" had 25 relations inside it, 8 out and 3 in. "The record as its own apparatus" had 24 inside, 6 out and 1 in. The owner reads a line that wants several unrelated accounts as a signal that it holds several inquiries. This decision adds two lines, `records-of-inquiry` and `record-as-apparatus`, and moves those two parts' 43 entries to them. Each entry keeps its other lines, with a history note, and five that answer, refine or object to an entry of nucleating-argument keep that line too. nucleating-argument keeps the three linked parts. Each line gets its synthesis. Rejected: one account over all five parts; keeping one line and tagging parts by a new field; a split into five. | Proposed |
| [ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md) v3 | An account the record holds only in parts, for a line or a part of one, gets a SYNTHESIS that restates it, so the account has an address: it adds nothing, and its standing is its components'; there is one account per scope, an account may integrate the accounts of its parts, and a line whose parts barely relate is a candidate to split | [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) began from a filing gap: an integration left with no address, so the record could not say what its current account is, nor check a later synthesis for drift. The admission test it added guards against importing a source's broad summary as one more claim. [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md)'s review reused that test to backfill the current-account view. There the common verdict was that a candidate's integration was already stated in its components' bodies and notes, and nothing was filed. That recreates the original gap: the nucleating-argument line has an account, scattered, and the view shows none. This decision gives such an account a SYNTHESIS (version 3: the scheme is now accounts only, ADR-084). It restates a line's account as the record holds it, maps every component, and adds nothing; its standing is its components', and the view sets it out under its line. The review files one when a candidate fails the claim test only because the record already holds its integration, and never when it fails on a free parameter, an error or a contradiction. There is one account per scope, a line or a part of one, not one per line, and a line's account may integrate its parts' accounts. When a line's parts barely relate, that is a signal to split the line, which is decided separately. The demonstration is the former nucleating-argument line: its account, split into part syntheses and a line synthesis over them, after the split of the line (ADR-082). Rejected: treating lines without a synthesis as findings only; admitting such accounts; a separate scheme. | Proposed |
| [ADR-084](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) | A SYNTHESIS is an account of a scope of the record's argument and asserts nothing of its own, and whatever adds to its components is a CLAIM: the admitted syntheses return to the claims they were, the admission test becomes the test for filing a claim whose premises are claims, and a claim's premises are claims again | [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md) gave syntheses a scheme. An entry earned a place in it by passing one of [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s admission routes. Asked what the admitted syntheses add, the record's answer was one proposition each, with a credence, a voice, a warrant and a defeater. Those are a CLAIM's fields. The owner observed that such an addition should be a claim, which is atomic however many premises it has. The owner also observed that the unadmitted accounts, which map a scope's components and add nothing, are what "synthesis" means. This decision makes SYNTHESIS the scheme of accounts only. Its status is whether the mapping is right. Its defeater is fidelity. It has no role, warrant, route or premises. Anything that adds to its components is a CLAIM, filed under [ADR-072](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md)'s rule. [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s routes become the way such a claim shows it has content of its own. The nine claims moved into the scheme are restored under their own codes, and the two syntheses that were never claims become new claims. A claim's `rests_on` names claims only again, so the patches [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) and [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md) made are undone. It supersedes [ADR-076](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-076.md), [ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md) and [ADR-080](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md), and amends [ADR-075](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md), [ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) and [ADR-083](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-083.md). Rejected: a field telling the two kinds apart within one scheme; the status quo; moving the integrations to new claim codes; an `integrates` field on CLAIM; making accounts generated views. | Proposed |
| [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) v2 | An entry carries every line whose argument it takes part in: the first line of each entry it answers, objects to or bears on, and of each question it refines, in one step; resting on or using an entry of another line is a dependency across lines, not participation, and stays a reported crossing | `line` takes several values, and a line is "a named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found" ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). Nothing said when an entry should carry a second line. [ADR-082](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) answered it for one case, the split of nucleating-argument: a moved entry keeps the old line when it answers, refines or objects to one of that line's entries. This decision makes the rule general and adds `bears_on`: an entry carries the first line of each entry it answers, objects to or bears on, and of each question it refines (version 2). A line the target carries second does not pass, and nothing cascades, so one pass is final. Resting on or using one does not count; that is a dependency the `argument` chain reports as a crossing, which is what [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) meant it to do. Neither does `complements` alone. The demonstration gives the line to the eleven entries among the lint's 79 cross-line steps that bear on a question of the premise's line. Version 2's sweep applies it record-wide. Rejected: counting `complements`; counting `rests_on`; every line a target carries; following the rule until nothing changes; leaving it to judgement entry by entry. | Proposed |
| [ADR-086](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-086.md) | An entry shows the accounts that integrate it: `integrates` gets a derived converse, `integrated_by`, on every scheme an account can integrate, so a part of a line's argument is visible from its members and not only from the current-account view | The synthesis reviews of 2026-11-10 divided lines into parts, each with an account, and kept some densely linked parts together in one line. The owner asked whether tags or some other abstraction express what such a cluster has in common. Measured, no `topics` tag both covers a part and is specific to it, because tags record what a work is about, at the grain of a field. Some parts hang from a root question or a hub claim, and six have none. The one thing that names every part is its account, and `integrates` runs one way: no entry shows which account it belongs to. This decision gives `integrates` a derived converse, `integrated_by`, declared on the seven schemes an account can integrate, and stored on no entry ([ADR-079](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-079.md)). On the record of 2026-11-10 it annotates 163 entries, 18 of them with two or more accounts. Rejected: cluster-level tags; a stored `part` field; leaving it to the current-account view. | Proposed |
| [ADR-087](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md) | The readiness line is split in two: readiness keeps keeping a rare capability and reaching and paying for configurations under budgets; when transient support can be withdrawn becomes the line transient-support, because that part barely relates to the other two | The synthesis review of 2026-11-10 gave readiness its first account, over three parts: keeping and judging a rare capability, reaching and paying for configurations under budgets, and withdrawing transient support. Counted by the line's 163 linked pairs, the first two share 28 and the third shares 5 and 1 with them; by stored relations, all three are mostly closed. Setting readiness aside would take the withdrawal inquiry with it, which is the opposite of what a line is for ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)). This decision adds the line transient-support, "Withdrawing transient support", and moves the 30 entries of the third part to it, in place of readiness. [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) keeps readiness beside it, because it bears on [QUESTION-386](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md) ([ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)). The part's account becomes the new line's, and readiness's line account is revised over its two remaining parts. It applies [ADR-082](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md)'s rule for a split. Rejected: one account over all three parts; splitting in three; moving the part into realizability. | Proposed |
| [ADR-088](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-088.md) | The withdrawal inquiry takes transient-support as its first line: its two root questions and the entries that argue them lead with transient-support, and carry realizability only where they bear on a realizability-first entry, which completes the split of readiness | [ADR-087](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md) split readiness and moved its withdrawal part to the new line transient-support, keeping each entry's other lines where they were. Its roots, [QUESTION-398](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) and [QUESTION-399](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md), kept realizability first. The synthesis review of 2026-11-11 found that part again inside realizability, closed off from the rest of it: its entries carry realizability chiefly because they bear on one of the two questions ([ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)). This decision gives both questions and the withdrawal entries transient-support as their first line, and keeps realizability on them only where [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) supplies it, through a relation to a realizability-first entry. None of them has one. Twenty-one entries change, and all leave realizability. Rejected: leaving the first lines as [ADR-087](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md) left them; keeping [QUESTION-399](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) in realizability; keeping realizability on every moved entry. | Proposed |
| [ADR-089](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-089.md) | Normative judgment about organizations becomes a line of its own, organizational-normativity, split from will-organization: whether an organization's own dynamics ground norms, and what judging one needs, is a question of its own, while acting as one stays, because its root question refines the line's own | The synthesis review of 2026-11-11 gave will-organization its first account, over six parts. Two parts were mostly closed: acting as one, and normative judgment about organizations. The owner left the split to the assistant's judgement. This decision adds the line organizational-normativity, "Normative judgment about organizations", and moves the 23 entries of the normative part to it in place of will-organization. Its root question asks whether an organization's own dynamics ground norms and what more judging one needs, which is not what organizes practical efficacy in an agent. Its ties to the line are two uses of a term and premises, which are dependencies. No relation supplies will-organization to any moved entry, and no entry outside the part gains the new line. Acting as one stays: its root question refines the line's own. Rejected: keeping both parts; splitting both; moving the normative part into distributed-agency or authenticity. | Proposed |
| [ADR-090](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-090.md) v2 | A reading takes the lines of the entries that use it, derived when the record is built and never stored, and a view lists each line's readings and the readings no line uses | A THEORY has no `line` field ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)), so nothing showed which lines of the argument a reading serves, and the synthesis reviews of 2026-11-11 found promotion conditions that link to nothing in their line because their links run to a THEORY. A reading's lines are now derived: the first lines of the entries that ground on it, that it corroborates, that it answers or bears on, or that it reports, leaving out entries Superseded or Rejected. They are computed when the views are built and stored nowhere, so they cannot drift. The view docs/readings-by-line.md, built from record/views.d/readings-by-line.md.j2, lists each line's readings and the readings in force that no line uses: on 2026-11-11, 406 of 856 serve a line and 450 serve none (version 2). Rejected: a stored `line` on THEORY; counting every line of a using entry. | Proposed |
| [ADR-091](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-091.md) | Readings no line uses are reviewed in a protocol of their own, by line, by topic or by question, and each is tied to an entry that should use it, raised as a question or claim, held with a reason, or flagged | [ADR-090](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-090.md) derives a reading's lines from the entries that use it, and its view shows 450 of 856 readings in force used by no line. The owner holds that the record should be building on its readings, and that reviewing under-used ones is worth its own protocol, maybe several. This decision makes it one protocol with three modes, carried by the reading-review skill: by line (what a line should build on), by topic (where the record reads and does not argue) and by question (evidence the argument has not weighed). Each reading reviewed gets one of four verdicts: tie it to an entry whose own text should use it, raise a question or claim it calls for, hold it with a reason, or flag a defect in it. The demonstration runs the by-line mode on organizational-normativity, the one line no reading served. Rejected: folding it into the synthesis review; three separate protocols; tying readings by topic alone. | Proposed |
| [ADR-092](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-092.md) | A case can bear on a question, by the same `bears_on` claims, readings and accounts carry, and a question's `bearing` lists the cases with them; how the case bears is its kind's to say, not the relation's | A CASE could point only at claims (`illustrates`, `counterexample_to`) and at other cases, so a case filed for a question could not say so: the defect sweeps of 2026-11-11 found a dozen cases whose text names the question they serve, and the case filed for [QUESTION-449](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md) could reach it only through its readings. A CASE now carries `bears_on`, to questions, with the meaning it has on a claim, and QUESTION's `bearing` converse takes cases. Whether a case tests, models or is an instance of the question is its `kind` ([ADR-042](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-042.md)), so one relation serves. [ADR-085](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md)'s line rule applies: a case takes the first line of a question it bears on. The demonstration adds the relation to the cases the sweeps found and to [CASE-232](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-232.md). Rejected: a relation per kind (tests, models, probes, examines); `motivates`; widening `illustrates` to questions. | Proposed |
| [ADR-093](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-093.md) | A reading named as evidence in a question's or claim's text is tied when the name is written, supporting cases corroborate, a question's instruments are its premises, and readings used only by cases, terms or syntheses are held as used | The first by-topic reading review (2026-11-11, five readers, 222 readings) found that most readings the view counted unused were already named as evidence in a question's or claim's text, with no relation written, and its readers met the same unsettled cases. This decision settles them for the reading review and for filing: a note that names a reading as evidence writes the relation; a claim's supporting cases, instances and in-scope precedents corroborate it; a question's named instruments, measures and cautions are premises it bears on; a reading tied to several entries is one verdict; a reading used only by a case, a term or a synthesis is held as used in fact; a claim grounding on a work that now has a reading gets the reading as corroboration or ground, and the LIT edge goes to a sweep; and a split run coordinates its raises. The reading-review and read-and-file skills carry the instructions. Rejected: a relation from a case, term or synthesis to a reading; stretching `reported_in` to cover use; leaving the cases to each reader. | Proposed |
| [ADR-094](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-094.md) | A reading that marks the limit of a claim's scope, cited as such in the claim's own text, carries `bounds` to the claim, and the claim's `bounded_by` is derived; it is neither support nor objection | Claims say what they do not cover, and often cite a reading to mark the limit: a regime where the result fails, a domain the claim does not reach, a case its own condition excludes. No relation recorded that use. `corroborates` is support and `objects_to` a rebuttal between claims; a limit is neither. On 2026-11-11, 114 pairs of a claim and a reading cited only in the claim's "What it does not say" section had no relation; the second by-topic reading review held such readings as taking nothing, and they showed as unused. A THEORY now carries `bounds` to the claims whose scope it marks, with the converse `bounded_by` derived on CLAIM; the readings view counts it as use. The demonstration writes it for the claims whose own text cites a reading as a limit. Rejected: leaving it in prose; a stored field on the claim; counting body citations as use by text search; `objects_to` or `corroborates` stretched to cover it. | Proposed |
| [ADR-095](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-095.md) | A case or a term that uses a reading other than as its source carries `draws_on` to it, and the reading's `drawn_on_by` is derived; how a case uses it is its kind's to say, and a term draws on the readings its sense is fixed by | A case reached a reading only by `reported_in`, which is provenance, and a term by nothing, so a proposed study that takes its measures and design constraints from readings, a construction built from a reading's result, and a term defined after a reading's usage recorded none of it. [ADR-093](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-093.md) had the reading reviews hold such readings as used in fact, and the owner deferred the relation to a decision of its own. On 2026-11-12, 156 citations of a reading in force by a case, and 153 by a term, carried no relation. CASE and TERM now carry `draws_on` to THEORY, with the converse `drawn_on_by` derived on THEORY; the readings view counts it as use. One relation serves both, as `bears_on` serves every scheme that bears on a question ([ADR-092](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-092.md)): a case's kind says how it uses the reading, and for a term it is the reading its sense is fixed by. The demonstration writes it where the case's or term's own text uses the reading. Rejected: a relation per use (method, constraint, check, component); stretching `reported_in`; leaving it to the reviews' accounts; extending it now to syntheses. | Proposed |
| [ADR-096](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-096.md) | A demonstrated claim whose argument rests on an explicit construction carries it as a construction case: `grounds` when the construction is what demonstrates the claim, `illustrates` when it is a worked instance of a general proof | On 2026-11-08 the owner told another assistant, about two claims it had proved by explicit constructions, to "make sure you connect the CLAIMs using those explicit constructions to CASEs describing them". The record has a construction kind of case ([ADR-042](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-042.md)), with 68 cases of it, but on 2026-11-12, 159 of its 221 demonstrated claims had no case grounding or illustrating them, and some of those carry a specific construction only in their body: [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s barrier at 1.3 is one, with two variants filed as cases and the example they alter filed as none. A construction in a claim's body cannot be cited, varied or reused by another entry. The decision: such a construction is filed as a case of kind construction, linked by `grounds` when it is what demonstrates the claim (an existence or separation claim) and by `illustrates` when the claim has a general proof the construction instances; a case that grounds a claim gets an ARG of form existence ([ADR-061](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md)). Taken up at a claim's next filing or review, not swept. Applied first to [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md). Rejected: a sweep of all 159 now; leaving constructions in bodies; a case for every proof; always `grounds`. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
